title: Toward Recursive Self-Improvement in Physical AI
abstract: arXiv:2610.29677v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) describes a system that improves not only its behavior but also the process by which it improves. Recent digital agents test this idea by rewriting their own code and checking each version with executable tests. Bringing these mechanisms into the physical world requires learning from partial observations through costly trials, while accounting for changing operating conditions and potentially irreversible consequences. We position RSI within robot learning and trace pathways from improving robot capabilities to improving the processes that generate them. We examine how physical experience can strengthen these improvement mechanisms and when the resulting gains can support further self-improvement of the mechanisms themselves. Gains carry forward only when feedback addresses remaining learning needs, the receiving component can use the change, its value survives changes in tasks or hardware, and continue

translated_title: 迈向物理人工智能中的递归自我改进
translated_abstract: 递归自我改进（RSI）描述了一种系统，它不仅改进自身的行为，还改进其进行自我改进的过程。近期的数字智能体通过重写自身代码并使用可执行测试检验每个版本来验证这一理念。将这些机制引入物理世界，需要通过代价高昂的试验从部分观测中学习，同时还要应对不断变化的运行条件和潜在的不可逆后果。我们将RSI置于机器人学习的框架内，并梳理了从改进机器人能力到改进生成这些能力的过程的路径。我们研究了物理经验如何能够强化这些改进机制，以及由此产生的收益何时能够支持机制本身进一步的自我改进。只有当反馈满足剩余的学习需求、接收组件能够利用该改变、其价值在任务或硬件变化中得以保留时，改进收益才能得以延续……（摘要原文在此截断）
tldr: 该论文首次将递归自我改进（RSI）系统性地引入物理AI与机器人学习领域，提出利用物理经验强化自我改进机制，并分析了改进收益得以延续并支撑机制进一步自我改进的必要条件。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces recursive self-improvement (RSI) into physical AI and robot learning, proposing that physical experience can strengthen self-improvement mechanisms and analyzing the conditions under which improvement gains can carry forward to enable further self-improvement of the mechanisms themselves.
